sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: crossing distances, gates, stalls, interstate ramps and light distances
Confusable pairs among the railroad crossing rules, interstate procedures and light distances, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
The stopping zone at a railroad crossing is between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail, closer than 15 being too near and farther than 50 too far. [A01]
Why it matters: group crossing distances; difficulty high; confusable minimum versus maximum.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
The audible-train trigger refers to a train within roughly 1500 feet, while the stopping zone itself is measured in tens of feet from the rail. [A01]
Why it matters: group crossing distances; confusable warning distance versus stopping distance.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A02
Before the signals start you stop short of the lowering gates, but if you are already on the tracks when they start you keep moving and do not stop or back up. [A02]
Why it matters: group gates; difficulty high; confusable approaching versus already crossing.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A02
At a crossbuck with flashing red lights you stop as for any flashing red signal, while at a crossbuck with no lights or gates you must still yield to any train. [A02]
Why it matters: group crossing controls; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A03
A stalled car on the tracks means get out and move away first, and only then call the railroad using the Blue Sign, not the other way round. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergencies; misconception target.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A03
The Blue Sign number reaches the railroad for crossing emergencies, while damaged or missing signs go to the Federal Railroad Administration. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergencies; dynamic; confusable railroad versus federal contact.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A05
On entry you speed up in the acceleration lane to match traffic, while on exit you move into the deceleration lane before slowing down. [A05]
Why it matters: group interstate ramps; difficulty medium; confusable entry versus exit.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A05
A breakdown calls for pulling far off the road with a white cloth and raised hood, and the interstate rule is never to stop in a travel lane. [A05]
Why it matters: group interstate stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A06
A missed exit is handled by driving on to the next one, while entering the wrong way is handled by pulling onto the right shoulder, stopping and turning around when clear. [A06]
Why it matters: group interstate errors; difficulty high; confusable missed exit versus wrong-way entry.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A06
High beams should reveal a person at 200 feet and low beams at 75 feet, while taillights must be visible at 500 feet and the plate light must light the numbers at 50 feet. [A06]
Why it matters: group light distances; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0067]
